articleTitle: Microstrip patch array for an active SAR demonstrator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: Reviews the development work carried out on the antenna for a microstrip patch array operating at 5300 MHz for an active SAR antenna. The work, carried out by Matra Marconi Space, covers the initial design leading up to the present working array. Details of the array and measured results are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simplified analysis of circular microstrip patches
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: The author shows how useful trigonometric approximations to Bessel functions can be employed to simplify the analysis of circular microstrip patches. Specifically, it is shown how the approximations in question can be used both at the design stage and in the expressions for the radiated far field components of such patches to enable quantities of physical interest to be examined with relative ease. With respect to the design equations, a modified cavity model method of analysis is adopted and the patch is assumed to be excited in the fundamental mode by, for example, a thin coaxial probe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model for the patch radiator with a perturbation to achieve circular polarization
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: Some models have been proposed for the equivalent circuit of the patch antenna with a perturbation (central slots, gaps at the edges etc. ) in order to get circular polarization. These models make, in some cases, a qualitative description of the behaviour of the patch but without foreseeing its behaviour concerning AR (axial ratio) and reflection coefficient, versus frequency, or in other cases their results are not accurate, in the authors' knowledge, in all the parameters mentioned. They propose a simple model allowing, starting from measurements of the patch alone or from its design parameters, them to foresee the optimum frequency at which circular polarization will be achieved by means of a perturbation (central slot or other), the AR versus frequency (and so the bandwidth in circular polarization) and even the reflection coefficient versus frequency (matching bandwidth). The model has been applied to several circular patches (at different frequencies, and with different thickness of substrates) showing a very good agreement with the experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of microstrip antennas at Alenia Spazio
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: In the frame of ESA studies, a programme concerning with the development of microstrip antennas for space applications was started at Alenia Spazio. Several types of technological solutions and radiators have been developed. An overview of the manufactured radiators together with the achieved measured results at S-band and VHF-band is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental investigation of large Microstrip array antenna design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: During the last years several research and development programmes have been carried out by Saab Ericsson Space in the field of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) antennas for space applications. The aim has been to develop and evaluate different design concepts for future SAR applications. The present generation of European spaceborn SARs (ERS-1 and ERS-2) uses a fixed beam antenna with slotted waveguides as radiators and a centralized receiver and transmitter. The next generation SAR systems require dual polarized antennas with steerable beams. Distributed T/R modules will be used, where each module feeds a dual polarized subarray. The paper presents the electrical analysis and design of a large C-band microstrip advanced SAR antenna (ASAR) developed for the European Space Agency. The paper also presents a recently developed method for predicting co- and cross-polar radiation from microstrip array antennas including spurious radiation from the associated microstrip feed line network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space environment problems for microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: Natural and induced space environments have important deleterious effects on space systems. Troublesome environments and their effects are summarised. The environment is extremely diverse in nature and the effects it causes are similarly varied. Charged particles are present at energies ranging from around the eV level up to MeVs and beyond. In addition, various neutral environments cause significant problems. All these environments have to be considered for new technologies such as microstrip antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: CASA jointly with TeDeCe has been developing in the last years wide applications of printed antennas. This has been based on the research and development of new materials ad configurations as carbon and glass fibres, kapton, kevlar, rohacell, diclad, etc. Those materials have been evaluated electrically as well as from the thermo/structural point of view, to assure good in-orbit behaviour, taking into account special space-flight problems like outgassing, ESD, radiation, PIMP, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the sinergy between space and ground developments of printed antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Developments in Microstrip Antennas
abstract: The explained set of requirements and constraints, for the use of microstrip patches led to define a special technology for printed arrays in space environment, based on the use of multilayer structures composed by low density foams and very thin printed boards assembled with spatially qualified adhesives; these ones must be reduced to a minimum, because of their influence on the RF losses. This technology is summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
